notes: Answer as one set covering 56 places: the 50 states, D.C., Puerto Rico, Guam, the U.S. Virgin Islands, American Samoa and the Northern Mariana Islands, plus the federal level.
Rules only, never observations. Where a state's law is not found, mark the field UNKNOWN rather than borrowing another state's rule.

lamontae's two decisions, recorded by ChatGPT on September 22, 2026 (docs/research/chatgpt-answers/2026-09-23-legislation-decisions-0122/): (1) 'Warn, then allow a lawful challenge': when a city proposes a measure whose authority is disputed, the city attorney warns the player and a lawful challenge may proceed; a clear, settled prohibition blocks enactment. (2) 'Yes, law first; effects when encountered': a passed bill first changes a concrete law, tax or budget record, and its effects reach people when the rule reaches them, such as the next tax collection or an actual violation. Neither decision says which subjects a given state preempts or what any place's law already says; those facts still come from this question, and an unknown rule is neither automatic permission nor automatic refusal. The question stays open.
question: What may each level of government legislate on, and what stops it? For Congress, each state legislature, the D.C. Council, each territorial legislature, and counties and cities in each state: (1) which kinds of act it passes (statute, ordinance, resolution, appropriation, tax levy, borrowing, constitutional or charter amendment) and what each is called there; (2) the subjects reserved to it or denied to it: federal enumerated powers and supremacy, what states may not do, and for local governments whether the state follows home rule or Dillon's rule and which subjects the state has preempted (firearms, minimum wage, rent control, plastic bags, taxes and so on are the usual examples); (3) what happens when a lower level passes something beyond its power: void on its face, struck down only if someone sues, or overridden by a later state law; (4) whether counties legislate at all in that state, and through what body (commission, board of supervisors, fiscal court, and so on); (5) for D.C., what Congress may review or overturn and on what schedule. Cite each provision and mark anything not found as UNKNOWN. Also, for every one of those acts once enacted: (6) what it actually changes in the world and when: a tax levy's rate, base, who collects it and when revenue arrives; an appropriation's amount, recipient and fiscal year; a borrowing's term; an ordinance's rule and its penalty; and which later record a player could see it in (a tax bill, a budget line, a citation).

readFirst.words: This legislative stuff, this is urgent. For ChatGPT, this needs to be built out. No federal laws, no only Alaska passing a tax bill. Nothing for cities. Or municipalities, whatever. That's ridiculous. And we need to make sure that this stuff is actually being tied to real world effects.

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: A bill is only general-policy, appropriation or revenue, a money-versus-policy split for vote thresholds. Nothing says what subjects a level may address.
127 issues record the levels that ordinarily decide them, but nothing reads that to allow or refuse a bill, and there is no federal level.
The fields exist as source data for fiscal authority only; no answer for non-fiscal subjects and no rule for what a lower level's overreach does.

title: What laws each level of government may pass, and what stops it
usableAnswer: One row per jurisdiction per level (federal; each of the 56 state-level places; that place's counties and cities as a rule, not per town) listing the act kinds with their local names, reserved and denied subjects, the local-power doctrine (home rule or Dillon's rule, with any statutory exceptions), preempted subjects, what happens to an act beyond a level's power, and a citation and evidence status for each field. For (6), one row per act kind per level with the fields that enacted law changes and a citation for each.
whyItMatters: Today the game never checks whether a subject belongs to the level passing it: a city could pass a state-level law and nothing would refuse it. Congress has seats but passes nothing, counties have no legislative body at all, and only one city (Charlottesville) has a working council route. Without the real division of powers, any limit the game adds would be invented. lamontae called this urgent on 2026-09-22 at 8:40 p.m. Eastern and asked that enacted laws be tied to real-world effects; the engine is being scaffolded now with marked placeholders, and each placeholder waits on this answer.

answer.summary: One nationwide set: Congress plus all 50 states, D.C. and the five inhabited territories, each with the cited source of its legislative power, the basis for local lawmaking where found, and UNKNOWN where not verified. Federal: Congress acts only within enumerated or otherwise vested powers (Article I, Section 8 and the Necessary and Proper Clause), bounded by Article I, Section 9 and the amendments; valid federal law is supreme and may preempt expressly, by field, or by conflict; states are barred by Article I, Section 10. D.C. Council acts go to Congress for a 30-day review (60 days for Titles 22 to 24) and take effect unless both houses pass a disapproval resolution signed by the President. Each territory has its own organic act or constitution and must not be inferred from D.C. or another territory. A recommended common record for every act separates what enactment changes (statute or ordinance, appropriation, tax levy, borrowing authorization, constitutional amendment) from the later records of its experienced effect: an appropriation is budget authority, not cash spent; a tax statute creates liability, not payment. Owner decisions carried in the file: governors and legislators pursue regular agendas driven by circumstances without the player; a clear settled prohibition blocks enactment, while a plausible dispute gives a warning and a lawful challenge; passage first changes a concrete law or budget record.

Territory local lawmaking (Guam villages, USVI, American Samoa village councils, CNMI district delegations) and most ultra vires procedures are UNKNOWN. Effective-date and finance mechanics are UNKNOWN until sourced per place and instrument. No frequency, success rate or policy mix for background agendas has been approved.
